```{=html}
<details id="home-map-notes" class="dashboard-reading-notes">
<summary>Reading these maps</summary>
<ul>
<li><strong>Reference and dates:</strong> PRISM ranks and departures use seasonally matched 1991&ndash;2020 comparisons. Low precipitation ranks mean drier conditions; high dry-spell ranks mean unusually long dry spells. Positive temperature departures mean warmer conditions, in &deg;F. Recent inputs are preliminary; use each map's data date.</li>
<li><strong>Water year:</strong> Precipitation starts October 1. Early-season ranks cover a short period; the 90-day map provides broader context.</li>
<li><strong>Regional values:</strong> Summaries cover Arizona and New Mexico, weighted by grid-cell area within state boundaries, and require at least 98% valid area. Percentile percentages describe affected area, not an average percentile. Each summary follows its map's period and date.</li>
<li><strong>Headline precipitation cards:</strong> Below-/above-normal area uses below percentile 33 / above percentile 67. Mixed shading retains both dry and wet signals.</li>
<li><strong>Very dry/wet map summaries:</strong> Affected area uses below percentile 10 / above percentile 90. Dry-spell summaries highlight the unusually long tail. Map-summary tooltips give the thresholds and dates.</li>
<li><strong>Summary color cues:</strong> Stronger precipitation or dry-spell summary colors highlight a larger affected area, not more extreme grid-cell values. Temperature summary colors show warmer/cooler departures, not statistical significance. Rainfall amounts remain neutral because amount alone does not establish rarity. These cues are not a combined drought classification.</li>
</ul><p><a href="pages/methods.html">About the data and methods</a></p></details>
<nav id="historic-seasons" class="dashboard-context-links" aria-label="Historical climate context">

</nav>
```
